title: The Morning Brief: Kushner meets Hamas as Netanyahu prepares to weigh road map
dek: The Trump administration opened direct talks with Hamas in Egypt on Sunday as part of a push to salvage a 15-point peace plan for Gaza, with the Israeli prime minister scheduled to meet Kushner on Monday. The day's major stories also brought developments in courts, military posture, and natural disaster response.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: Kushner's meeting with Hamas and the scheduled Netanyahu session represent the opening tests of whether the U.S. road map can move past the sequencing disagreements that have stalled negotiations, ahead of an Israeli election in October.
bottom_line: Kushner's meeting with Hamas and the Netanyahu session scheduled for Monday open a critical window for the U.S. road map to advance, though the reporting does not establish what private signals either side has sent. The Supreme Court's final rejection of Trump's $5 million Carroll appeal closes that litigation avenue; the $83 million verdict appeal remains pending. Trump's order to reduce South Korea exercises and his characterization of North Korea shift alliance posture in East Asia, with the Pentagon's implementation details and South Korea's official response still unknown. An earthquake killing at least 53 in Indonesia has triggered a significant aftershock sequence that will determine whether rescue teams can reach remote settlements and whether the death toll rises.
body: The central story of the morning is a high-stakes diplomatic gambit unfolding in real time. On Sunday in Egypt, Jared Kushner met directly with Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya, alongside envoys Nickolay Mladenov and Tony Blair, with representatives from Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey present. The desk reported the session focused on concrete actions toward Hamas disarmament, Israeli troop withdrawal from Gaza, and humanitarian relief. Kushner is scheduled to meet Netanyahu on Monday, setting up a sequential test of whether both sides will shift from their public positions. Netanyahu rejected the road map last week, and eight Muslim-majority nations issued a joint statement condemning Israel's rejection. The reporting does not specify what, if any, concessions either side has signaled privately.

Elsewhere on the day's record: the Supreme Court declined for a second time to hear Trump's appeal of the $5 million Carroll verdict, leaving that judgment final and the $5.62 million payment complete. A separate $83 million verdict from a 2024 trial remains in the appeals process. Trump on Sunday ordered the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, citing cost and characterizing North Korea as unthreatening during his tenure. The exercises, involving 18,000 South Korean soldiers over 11 days, were scheduled to begin this week. The reporting does not detail what "substantially reduce" will entail operationally, and South Korea has not yet officially responded.

Court documents show that Camron Harris, 19, the alleged shooter in the Virginia State University incident that wounded five people Saturday, sent Instagram messages saying "I'm tryna find the gun" and "We js got the shootin," indicating real-time documentation of acquiring and using a firearm. He faces multiple felony charges and remains in custody.

In Indonesia, a 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Flores Island on August 16, killing at least 53 people and triggering nearly 1,000 aftershocks, the largest measuring 6.2 magnitude. A 6.4-magnitude quake struck Sumatra Island the same day. Rescuers recovered 47 bodies on Saturday and six more on Sunday. About 5,000 people were displaced into temporary shelters. Search and rescue operations continue in a region where landslides and power outages have constrained communication and access to remote villages.
